cases.question: I use my phone on the Tube and a contactless card on the bus. Do I need to do anything differently when I change between them?
essential_points: Use the same card or device for the whole rail journey; a phone and its linked physical card count as different payment identities.
Touch in and out on rail, but touch in only on a bus.
cases.rationale: Tests a concise explanation of payment identity and the different rail/bus touch rules without an unnecessary map pin. Grounded in tfl-payment-1 and tfl-payment-2.

cases.question: We will make two bus journeys in London on 31 October 2026, about 40 minutes apart. What fare rule should I know, and is the announced November change already in effect?
essential_points: The Hopper gives unlimited bus and tram journeys within one hour of the first touch-in using the same card or device; it is automatic.
On 31 October the adult single is £1.75 and daily cap £5.25; announced £1.85 and £5.55 fares start 1 November, not in October.
cases.rationale: Checks date-sensitive fare advice and the automatic one-hour transfer rule without mapping a non-place question. Grounded in tfl-bus-fares-1 and tfl-bus-fares-2.

cases.question: I'm visiting with an 8-year-old and a 13-year-old. How do their London bus and Tube fares differ, and what should I arrange for the older child?
essential_points: Under-11s travel free on buses and trams, and up to four under-11s can travel free with each fare-paying adult on specified TfL rail services; do not generalise this to all airport or National Rail services.

A visitor aged 11–15 can get half-price travel with the Young Visitor discount added to a Visitor Oyster by staff or a Visitor Centre while the child is present; it is not automatic on ordinary contactless.
cases.rationale: Tests age-specific family advice with a useful next step and the scope limit on free child rail travel. Grounded in tfl-children-1 and tfl-children-2.

cases.question: After a show, can I count on the Night Tube to get home on a Tuesday, and what is the rule for booking a minicab?
essential_points: Night Tube and Night Overground operate on Friday and Saturday nights, not every night; night buses are another overnight option, and the actual service for the date and destination needs checking.
A minicab/private-hire vehicle must be booked through a licensed operator; only licensed black taxis can be hailed or taken from a rank without a prior booking.
cases.rationale: Combines a night-service schedule rule with a practical licensed-vehicle distinction, with no location needing a pin. Grounded in tfl-night-1 and tfl-night-2.

cases.question: I'm taking a space-loving child to the Science Museum on 27 October 2026. What should I plan for admission and the published opening time?
essential_points: General admission is free, but visitors are asked to pre-book a free ticket; some experiences or exhibitions have separate tickets.
The published half-term opening for 24–30 October 2026 is 09:00; this is dated published information, not a live check.
cases.rationale: Tests date-bounded museum hours, free admission versus booking, and one correct venue anchor. Grounded in science-museum-1 and science-museum-2.

cases.question: It's forecast to rain and I have a dinosaur-mad child; should we spend our short afternoon at the Natural History Museum or the Science Museum?
essential_points: The Natural History Museum is the better match for dinosaur interests and is an indoor option; its galleries have free admission, but busy periods can queue without a free entry ticket.
The nearby Science Museum also has free general admission but asks visitors to pre-book; some experiences are separately ticketed.
Suggest prioritising one museum for a short afternoon rather than promising time to see both.
cases.rationale: Tests interest-led choice under a time constraint, concise booking nuance, and relevant multi-venue pins. Grounded in natural-history-1, natural-history-2, and science-museum-1.

cases.question: I like art and design and want an easy indoor stop in South Kensington. Does the V&A need a general-entry booking, and is its Fashion Gallery open?
essential_points: V&A South Kensington general admission is free and does not need booking; some exhibitions or events cost extra.
The Fashion Gallery is closed for redevelopment until autumn 2028 according to the visit page checked 23 October 2026.
cases.rationale: Tests a practical venue recommendation with a dated closure and the distinction between general entry and paid exhibitions. Grounded in va-museum-1 and va-museum-3.

cases.question: Would Borough Market work for a Sunday lunch, and what should I expect to pay for entry versus the food?
essential_points: Borough Market is free to enter, while food and purchases cost money.
Its regular Sunday hours are 10:00–16:00, subject to holiday or festive exceptions; do not claim live opening has been checked.
cases.rationale: Tests concise day-specific market advice and separates free entry from purchase costs, with a single venue pin. Grounded in borough-market-1 and borough-market-2.

cases.question: We want a free, relaxed outdoor break between indoor sightseeing stops. Which central parks would suit a quiet walk or picnic?
essential_points: Hyde Park and Kensington Gardens are central Royal Park options for outdoor time, gardens, and a quieter change from indoor attractions.
The parks are free to explore; attractions, events, and facilities inside them may have separate charges or opening policies.
cases.rationale: Tests a simple preference-led recommendation for two relevant outdoor places and the boundary around charges inside parks. Grounded in royal-parks-1.

cases.question: Suggest a riverside stroll for a visitor with a couple of hours who wants to see the National Theatre and finish near Tate Modern.
essential_points: Queen’s Walk is the pedestrian promenade along the South Bank; a suggested sequence can include the National Theatre and continue toward Bankside/Tate Modern.
The roughly 30-minute published estimate applies from Lambeth Bridge to Blackfriars Bridge without extended stops, and individual pace varies.
Present this as a suggested itinerary, not turn-by-turn directions or a guaranteed accessible route.
cases.rationale: Tests a short multi-stop itinerary, map selection for requested places, and careful use of a bounded walking-time estimate. Grounded in south-bank-1 and south-bank-2.

cases.question: My family is interested in ships and maritime history. How could we spend a day around Greenwich, and which parts have free general entry?
essential_points: Royal Museums Greenwich includes the National Maritime Museum, Queen’s House, Cutty Sark, and Royal Observatory.
National Maritime Museum and Queen’s House have free general entry; Cutty Sark and Royal Observatory are ticketed attractions. Suggest booking ahead where possible and checking date availability.
Greenwich Park can complement a suggested day out; walking uphill to the Observatory is not an audited step-free route.
cases.rationale: Tests a family-interest itinerary with mixed admission types and four relevant destination/context pins, without inventing current ticket availability. Grounded in greenwich-museums-1 and greenwich-museums-2.

cases.question: I want a free view in the City and might also walk across Tower Bridge. Which of those can I do without buying an attraction ticket, and what needs booking?
essential_points: Sky Garden offers free public access tickets bookable up to three weeks ahead, specifying a date/time and one-hour visit; weekend booking is recommended and walk-ins depend on capacity.
The public pedestrian crossing of Tower Bridge is free; its interior/high-level exhibition is separately ticketed.
Do not claim ticket availability or a live bridge-lift schedule.
cases.rationale: Tests contrasting two kinds of free access, booking nuance, and multiple venue anchors while avoiding unsupported claims of availability. Grounded in sky-garden-1 and tower-bridge-1.
